$comment: The script is TypeScript syntax with raw strings (docs/script-syntax.md). This grammar is VS Code's TypeScript grammar plus an injection for the places the script differs. The injection applies inside every TypeScript rule (blocks, calls, arrays, ...), and its L: priority makes its rules win over TypeScript's at the same position, so TypeScript's own strings never start. It stays out of comments, strings, the JavaScript of script(() => ...) lambdas and the arguments of command(...).
name: RPG Maker MV Script

raw-fallback.$comment: Spec 7.7: command(code, parameters). The parameters are a JavaScript literal whose strings do use JavaScript escapes, so TypeScript's own rules read them.
raw-fallback.name: meta.function-call.raw-fallback.rpgmv-script

script-lambda.$comment: Spec 8.2: script(() => ...) and the move-route step .script(() => ...), whose lambda body is JavaScript kept as stored. The TypeScript rules read the lambda as they would any code; the injection stays out of it, so its strings are JavaScript strings. The call is only matched when a lambda follows its ( on the same line, or when the line breaks after the ( (a long lambda; a long string is still read as a raw string there). A step's dot must follow a ) or start the line, as TypeScript's call rule starts there too and would otherwise stay open; plugin.script(...) is a plugin command. script("..."), the fallback for code that can't be a lambda, is plain raw strings.

patterns.$comment: Starts before the whitespace, so it wins over TypeScript's arrow rule when the lambda starts a line.
patterns.name: meta.script-lambda.rpgmv-script

string.$comment: Spec 4.4: raw strings. A backslash never escapes, so a string ends at the first matching quote on its line. A backtick string is not a template.

text-code.$comment: Spec 4.5, kept in step with CODE in packages/core/src/text-codes.ts: \\ first, then \G (even before more letters), then letters with an optional [argument], then one symbol. Codes the core engine defines are text-code; others (from plugins) are text-code.unknown. A backslash that starts no code is plain text.
